name: How do carpenters handle uneven walls and crooked corners in older Denver homes?

mainEntity.name: How do carpenters handle uneven walls and crooked corners in older Denver homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older Denver-area homes, settling over decades often creates uneven floors, out-of-square corners, and wavy plaster or drywall. Installing straight, rigid trim against uneven surfaces requires skilled scribing—shaving the back edge of moldings to follow wall contours—rather than forcing wood flat. Standard 45-degree corner cuts rarely fit older walls, so carpenters use coped joints on inside corners to allow trim to fit cleanly despite imperfect angles. Abraham Becerra and the HH Remodeling crew handle these structural quirks during renovations, adjusting door jambs and casing profiles so new woodwork looks straight and level.
acceptedAnswer.description: Carpenters use coped inside joints and scribe moldings to trace wall contours, ensuring tight, straight fits even against uneven or settled walls.
